text_blocks.snippet: Common scams active in Central Illinois include fake law enforcement threats, jail or GPS release demands, and seasonal rental or weather contractor fraud.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake law enforcement threats, jail or GPS release demands, and seasonal rental or weather contractor fraud

list.snippet: Fake Police and Court Texts/Calls: Scammers pose as the Illinois State Police, county sheriffs, or court officials threatening immediate legal action, arrest warrants, or fines unless you click a link or pay via gift cards, Zelle, or cryptocurrency .
Jail and GPS Monitoring Scams: Imposters call claiming a loved one is arrested or needs money for GPS electronic monitoring supervision to stay out of jail.
Rental Fraud: Scammers target college move-in seasons by copying real property listings online to steal deposits and first month's rent from students.
Severe Weather / Contractor Scams: Following heavy storms or hail, unverified solicitors use high-pressure tactics demanding immediate contract signatures for home repairs.
Extortion & Sextortion Emails: Scammers send emails listing your real name, address, and street view alongside fake threats to release explicit media unless paid in Bitcoin.
Never pay over the phone: Legitimate law enforcement, government agencies, utilities, and courts never demand immediate payment via gift cards, crypto, or prepaid cards.
Verify independently: Hang up and call official local numbers or check state websites directly rather than using links or phone numbers provided in suspicious texts.
Slow down on contracts: Research local companies thoroughly and refuse to sign high-pressure repair contracts on the spot after storms.
